overview: Spicy's Fly is a settings-heavy module with four modes: a plain Vanilla capabilities fly, a Hypixel mode built on the damage-then-hover cycle with packet buffering, and HypixelFast1 and HypixelFast2, which launch the player with a stack of position packets to simulate fall damage and then fly on a decaying speed value. The module's packet handler is the notable part: in Hypixel mode every outgoing C03 is rewritten to claim onGround false and moving false, every other packet is optionally buffered in a blink list while fallDistance stays under 3, and the buffered packets are flushed on disable through sendPacketNoEvent so the server never sees the gap. An S08 teleport counter (hypixelLagback) tracks how many teleports arrive, and a timer-speed boost raises ticksPerSecond to 27.

sections.p: onEnable branches on the mode: Vanilla stores the original fly speed and lifts the player half a block, Hypixel jumps, zeroes stepHeight and arms the damage state, and both fast modes call onEnableHypixelFastfly1, which stacks C04 position packets every 0.0625 blocks to simulate a fall of 3 plus the damage value (1 for Fast1, 0.85 for Fast2) and then zeroes motion and jumpMovementFactor. onDisable restores stepHeight, resets fly capabilities, flushes the buffered packet lists through sendPacketNoEvent, and optionally stops motion. The module's onEvent dispatches on the mode: the fast modes get their own handlers, the Hypixel mode gets an EventSendPacket branch that rewrites C03 packets and buffers everything else, and an EventMotion branch runs the hover cycle.

The Hypixel hover cycle is a three-stage position dance. While hypixelDamaged is true, the module sets onGround true and motionY 0.0 client-side, computes two offsets (a fixed 8.24934E-9 and a jittered value around 4.496E-4 or 4.496E-43), and cycles a hypixelStage counter: stage 0 re-asserts the position, stage 1 shifts y down by the jittered offset when airborne, stage 2 shifts y up by the same offset, then resets. Every outgoing C03 in the mode is rewritten with setMoving(false) and setIsOnGround(false), and when hypixelBlink is on and fallDistance is under 3, every non-keepalive packet is parked in hypixelPackets and cancelled; a fallDistance of 3 or more triggers a motion boost at hypixelBoostSpeed. The timer boost runs ticksPerSecond at 27 whenever enabled.

The fast modes fly on a decaying speed value. onEventHypixelFastfly1 zeroes all motion in air, computes speedf from the hypixelFastFly1Speed setting plus speedAndStuff divided by the decay setting, and runs a five-stage position cycle that nudges y up by a tiny offset (1.42E-14) for four stages and re-asserts on the fifth, with an optional blink that buffers all non-keepalive packets while damaged. onEventHypixelFastfly2 is a simpler variant: it only acts when fallDistance is at least 3, applying a 4.0 motion boost and the same y nudge cycle. The Verus remnant in the mode list sets onGround true and motionY 0.0 on every update, and the onSettingChange handler reshuffles which settings are visible based on the active mode.

files.label: Fly.java (module)
files.explanation:
The entire module is this one file. onEnable arms the mode: Vanilla saves and overrides the fly capability speed, Hypixel jumps and zeroes stepHeight, and the fast modes call onEnableHypixelFastfly1, which stacks C04 position packets in 0.0625-block steps to simulate the fall damage that arms the fly state. The main onEvent method dispatches the fast modes to their own handlers, runs the Hypixel EventSendPacket branch (C03 onGround/moving rewrites plus the optional blink buffering), and the EventMotion branch executes the three-stage hover cycle with the two offsets.

The packet traffic is the most interesting part of the file. In Hypixel mode, every outgoing C03PacketPlayer is mutated to setIsOnGround(false) and setMoving(false) before it reaches the wire, so the server never sees a grounded claim; when hypixelBlink is on and fallDistance is under 3, every packet except C00 keepalives, the handshake and login start is parked in the static hypixelPackets list and cancelled, then flushed through sendPacketNoEvent on disable. The S08 teleport counter (hypixelLagback) increments per teleport and the damage tracker (hypixelDamaged) arms the whole cycle from the health drop after the jump.

The fast modes are self-contained: onEventHypixelFastfly1 runs the motion-zeroing loop with the decaying speed and the five-stage y nudge, onEventHypixelFastfly2 acts only at fallDistance 3 or more with a 4.0 boost, and both have their own blink lists and disable flush paths. The file also carries the settings plumbing, including the onSettingChange handler that moves settings in and out of the visible list as the mode changes.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly compares every move against a physics envelope rebuilt from the world. The horizontal allowance comes from a speed estimation based on sprint and potions, the vertical allowance from vDistRel, which inherits momentum from the previous move and only accepts a zero-y move on ground, a jump, a step-up or a riptide launch, and ground is derived from a block ray trace rather than the packet flag. A violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back.

The fast-mode launch is caught by the vertical side first. The damage-stack floods C04 packets in 0.0625-block steps, which are individually tiny, but the launch is followed by sustained flight with motion zeroed in air, and the hover envelope has no momentum to inherit, so the airborne zero-y state is a violation. The Hypixel mode's offsets (8.24934E-9 and ~4.496E-4) are below any named envelope: the vertical movement is neither a jump nor a step-up, and the client-side onGround true is ignored because NCP ray-traces the position and finds air. The horizontal speed, which the module carries near the sprint prediction, is legal on its own, but the vertical profile alone produces yDistanceAboveLimit every tick.

The packet rewrites make it worse. Because every outgoing C03 is rewritten to onGround false and moving false, the server-side player is always mid-air, so SurvivalFly's set-back logic has a clear airborne trajectory to measure. The timer boost to 27 ticks per second changes the tick cadence the envelope assumes, compounding the discrepancy. The Vanilla capabilities fly is caught by the same physics comparison, and the 0.5-block lift on enable is a small but unexplained vertical move.

countering.label: Flight (hover, ascension, glide)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Flight checks the vertical profile of every move. The hover check fires when both the last and current vertical speeds are exactly 0.0 and airTicks passes maxHover, which is the Hypixel mode's resting state: motionY is zeroed every tick while airborne, so the vertical speed is 0.0 tick after tick and the hover flag fires once the air-time threshold is crossed. The sub-pixel offsets do not register as vertical speed in the motion components, so they neither reset the hover timer nor look like legal motion.

The ascension branch compares the rising vertical speed against the jump cap. The fast modes' motion boost of 4.0 at fallDistance 3 or more is roughly ten times the jump cap and flags ascending_too_fast on the first rising move, and the decaying speedf, while moderate, still exceeds the cap while it decays. The launch stack itself is a fast series of small C04 moves that Arc's move processing sees as a continuous rapid ascent, tripping the ascension counter. The descend branch requires the vertical change to match a gravity-derived polynomial; the module's instant motion zeroing after the boost produces vertical changes that never match the expected curve.

The Hypixel mode's health-drop arming is visible to the check as a jump (legal), but everything after it is flight outside the envelope. The one mode that partially survives is Vanilla, whose capabilities fly moves at the configured speed with a real vertical profile, but even that exceeds the jump cap while ascending at the speed setting, and the 0.5-block enable lift is unexplained.

countering.label: Fly (predicted-velocity discrepancy)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Fly runs a per-player vertical simulation. In air it predicts the next velocity as (previous estimated velocity - 0.08) * 0.98 and integrates it into an estimated position; the reported Y is compared against that estimate, and any discrepancy over 0.0001 is punished with a rubberband set-back. The Hypixel mode's sub-pixel offsets are the textbook failure: offsets around 4.496E-4 and smaller are far below the predicted gravity decay of about 0.0784 per tick, so the estimate and the report diverge on the first tick, and the zeroed motionY hover diverges from the predicted fall within a tick or two.

The fast modes fail the integrator harder. The launch stack of C04 packets produces a reported position that climbs rapidly while the simulation predicts a fall, separating the estimate from the report by the full launch distance, and the 4.0 motion boost at fallDistance 3 is an instant multi-block ascent. The packet buffering in blink mode makes it worse: while packets are parked, the server sees no updates at all, and Hawk's no-move tolerance of 20 ticks without a position update is exhausted by the buffering window, after which the flush lands the accumulated movement at once.

The landing check is the final catch. When the client reports onGround, the reported Y must fall between the previous Y and the estimated position, and the module's client-side onGround true with a mid-air position fails that window every time. The rewritten C03 packets, which always claim onGround false, keep the player permanently airborne in Hawk's view, so the estimated position and the reported position only diverge further. The 27 ticks-per-second timer boost changes the tick cadence the integrator assumes, compounding the discrepancy on every tick.
